title: Grade 7 Lessons 4 6
description: Grade 7 multiple-choice question bank. Each question has four options and one correct answer.

questions.question: What is the main goal of a phishing attack on internet users?

options.text: To improve a computer's performance
To create a backup of personal files
To block all advertisements
To trick people into revealing sensitive information or clicking harmful links

questions.question: Which term describes software installed without a victim's knowledge to harm a device?

options.text: Malware
Spreadsheet
Firewall
Web browser

questions.question: Why do hackers steal someone's identity online?

options.text: To make the person's internet faster
To impersonate the person, access accounts, commit fraud, or misuse personal information
To improve the person's online profile
To help the person remember passwords

questions.question: What does a DDoS attack mainly do to a website or network?

options.text: It makes the website's design more attractive
It creates a backup of the website
It overwhelms the service with traffic from many devices so legitimate users cannot access it
It safely removes viruses from the network

questions.question: You receive an email urging you to click a link to verify your bank account immediately. What should you do?

options.text: Click the link quickly
Reply with your password
Forward the email to all your friends
Do not click the link; contact the bank through its official website or phone number

questions.question: Imagine your laptop starts running very slowly after you open an unknown email attachment. What most likely happened?

options.text: The attachment may have installed malware on the laptop
The laptop has automatically upgraded its memory
The email has increased the internet speed
The keyboard has changed its language

questions.question: Your school's website suddenly stops working because thousands of unknown devices send it traffic at once. What is this called?

options.text: A software update
A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack
A normal search request
A password reset

questions.question: Which sequence correctly shows the typical stages of identity theft?

options.text: Return the identity → create a password → delete the account
Create a profile → update software → install a printer
Obtain someone's personal information → use it to impersonate them or access accounts → misuse it
Send a greeting → browse a website → close a browser

questions.question: Viruses, worms, and ransomware are all examples of which type of cybercrime?

options.text: Online shopping
Copyright protection
Video conferencing
Malware-related cybercrime

questions.question: The WannaCry attack in 2017 is best classified as which type of cybercrime?

options.text: Ransomware attack
Online auction fraud
Identity verification
Website design attack

questions.question: What does the term “inappropriate content” mean in an online context?

options.text: Information that is always suitable for every age
Material that may be harmful, offensive, unsafe, or unsuitable for certain users
A computer program used for drawing
A website that contains only school lessons

questions.question: Most social media platforms require users to be at least what age to sign up?

options.text: 5 years old
10 years old
13 years old, although requirements vary by platform and country
21 years old on every platform

questions.question: Which organization works specifically to remove child sexual abuse material from the internet?

options.text: A local sports club
A computer hardware shop
A general online shopping company
The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF)

questions.question: What is the main function of web content filter software?

options.text: To block or restrict access to selected websites or online content
To increase the speed of every computer
To create social media accounts
To automatically publish photos

questions.question: Imagine a classmate shows you a website that encourages dangerous behavior. What is the best response?

options.text: Share it with more classmates
Leave the website and tell a trusted adult or teacher
Follow the instructions on the website
Post your personal information there

questions.question: Your parents install software on your computer to monitor and limit certain online content. What is this software called?

options.text: Presentation software
Spreadsheet software
Parental control or content-filtering software
Video-editing software

questions.question: A child has gone missing and may be at risk online. Which organization would best help with this case?

options.text: A music streaming service
A computer games company
An online auction website
The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)

questions.question: A 13-year-old wants to create a YouTube account. What condition usually applies?

options.text: They may be able to use YouTube, but age requirements and parental supervision rules depend on the country and account type
They can use any online service without age restrictions
They must share their password publicly
They must create an account using a stranger's identity

questions.question: CEOP, IWF, and NCMEC are similar. What do they all mainly aim to do?

options.text: Sell computer equipment
Help protect children from online exploitation and abuse, and support reporting or action against harmful material
Provide online banking services
Create games for children

questions.question: Which of these best describes a person's digital footprint?

options.text: The physical marks left by shoes near a computer
A list of files stored only on a USB drive
The trail of information a person leaves through online activities
A computer's electricity usage

questions.question: Why does a website store HTTP cookies?

options.text: To physically clean the computer
To replace the computer's operating system
To prevent all websites from collecting information
To remember information such as preferences, sessions, and browsing activity

questions.question: Why is it recommended to delete old, unused online accounts?

options.text: To reduce the amount of personal information exposed and lower security risks
To make every website load more slowly
To remove the need for internet access
To make old passwords public

questions.question: What does a VPN mainly help protect while using public Wi-Fi?

options.text: The physical screen from scratches
The privacy of internet traffic by encrypting the connection between the device and VPN service
The device from running out of battery
The user's files from being deleted by mistake

questions.question: You are preparing your profile before a college or job application. What should you do to improve your digital footprint?

options.text: Post personal arguments publicly
Use an offensive username
Review old posts and share appropriate, positive, and accurate information
Share your passwords to prove you are trustworthy

questions.question: An employer searches your name online before an interview. What is most likely being reviewed?

options.text: Your computer's screen size
Your private files stored offline
The number of apps on your phone
Your public online presence and digital footprint

questions.question: You need to check your bank account using free Wi-Fi at a cafe. What is the safest thing to do?

options.text: Use your mobile network or a trusted VPN and ensure you are on the bank's official secure website
Use any banking link sent by a stranger
Save your password on the public computer
Leave your account signed in when you finish

questions.question: Which order of actions would best help improve your digital footprint over time?

options.text: Post everything publicly → ignore privacy → keep unused accounts
Review existing posts and accounts → remove or update unsuitable content → use privacy settings → share responsibly in future
Share passwords → accept every friend request → disable security
Create more accounts → reuse old passwords → ignore account settings

questions.question: If clearing your browser cookies reduces tracking, what is a likely trade-off?

options.text: The computer will no longer need software updates
All websites will become unavailable permanently
Some websites may forget preferences or sign you out, so you may need to log in again
Your online identity will be erased completely

questions.question: What do positive and negative digital footprint examples have in common?

options.text: They are always created intentionally
They can only be seen by the person who created them
They disappear as soon as a browser closes
They are traces of a person's online activity that may affect how others view them
